title: Programmable graph topology as a functional architecture code
hypothesis: A compact graph-program code reuses one shared node-function substrate to express several graph architectures, preserving heldout program outputs with fewer complete bytes and less active compute than independent graph networks and native sparse routing metadata.

world.teacher: same node functions under per-program directed sparse graph topologies
world.heldout: two topologies withheld from output scoring but programs stored at inference

fresh.release_rule: Keep fresh sealed after exact native sparse-routing alias or storage/quality gate miss.

controls: independent dense adjacency and node-function payloads
shared node functions plus native sparse edge indices
metrics: actual serialized bytes including graph metadata
success_gate: heldout nRMSE <=0.02, >=25% fewer complete bytes than independent, strict storage/compute gain over native sparse edge-index control.
failure_gate: FAIL if Mirror aliases native sparse routing or misses full-byte/compute frontier.

compute.operation_count: one message operation per active directed edge per layer

boundaries: Synthetic linear graph programs only; no GrapNet reproduction or learned architecture claim.
Heldout topology IDs and edge lists are stored in inference payload; this is not topology generalization.
No fresh worlds after development alias or gate failure.
